# Release versions for the Saltmarsh toolkit

The release engineers of the Saltmarsh toolkit use a house version scheme. `release(version, command)` checks versions, compares them and computes the next version.

## Versions

A **version** is `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, optionally followed by a pre-release part `-CHANNEL.N`. Numbers (`MAJOR`, `MINOR`, `PATCH`, `N`) are written in decimal with ASCII digits, no sign, no leading zeros (`0` itself is fine), and may not exceed 9999. `N` is at least 1. `CHANNEL` is one of `dawn`, `noon`, `dusk`, in this order from **lowest to highest**. Examples: `1.4.0`, `0.9.12-dawn.3`. Nothing else is a version (no blanks, no `v` prefix, no build metadata).

**Precedence** (used by `cmp`): compare `MAJOR`, then `MINOR`, then `PATCH` numerically; if they are all equal a version **without** a pre-release part is greater than one with it; two pre-release versions compare by channel order, then by `N`.

## Commands

`version` is validated first: if it is not a version the result is `error: version`, whatever the command is. The `command` text is split at **single spaces** (so a doubled or trailing space gives an unknown command). Commands:

* `check`: the result is `ok`.
* `cmp OTHER`: exactly one more word. If `OTHER` is not a version the result is `error: other`; otherwise `less`, `equal` or `greater` (is `version` less than, equal to or greater than `OTHER`).

Any other command (an unknown word, the wrong number of words, a command this version does not offer, wrong case) gives `error: command`. Results are plain text without a trailing newline.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/releaser.js`:

```
function release(version, command)  // returns a string; exported with module.exports
```

* `version`: the version text
* `command`: the command, e.g. `check`, `cmp 1.2.3`
* returns the result text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

| version | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| `7.6.16` | `check` | `ok` |
| `10.11.2` | `cmp 9.4.7` | `greater` |
| `3.0.8` | `check` | `ok` |

Run the visible tests with `node --test test/*.test.js`.

# Release versions for the Hollin planner

The release engineers of the Hollin planner use a house version scheme. `release(version, command)` checks versions, compares them and computes the next version.

## Versions

A **version** is `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, optionally followed by a pre-release part `-CHANNEL.N`. Numbers (`MAJOR`, `MINOR`, `PATCH`, `N`) are written in decimal with ASCII digits, no sign, no leading zeros (`0` itself is fine), and may not exceed 9999. `N` is at least 1. `CHANNEL` is one of `nightly`, `preview`, `candidate`, in this order from **lowest to highest**. Examples: `1.4.0`, `0.9.12-nightly.3`. Nothing else is a version (no blanks, no `v` prefix, no build metadata).

**Precedence** (used by `cmp`): compare `MAJOR`, then `MINOR`, then `PATCH` numerically; if they are all equal a version **without** a pre-release part is greater than one with it; two pre-release versions compare by channel order, then by `N`.

## Commands

`version` is validated first: if it is not a version the result is `error: version`, whatever the command is. The `command` text is split at **single spaces** (so a doubled or trailing space gives an unknown command). Commands:

* `check`: the result is `ok`.
* `cmp OTHER`: exactly one more word. If `OTHER` is not a version the result is `error: other`; otherwise `less`, `equal` or `greater` (is `version` less than, equal to or greater than `OTHER`).
* `major`: `MAJOR+1.0.0`. `minor`: `MAJOR.MINOR+1.0`. Both drop any pre-release part.
* `patch`: if the version has a pre-release part, only that part is dropped (the version *graduates*: `1.2.4-preview.2` becomes `1.2.4`); otherwise `PATCH` is increased by one.
  Any bump that would make a number exceed 9999 gives `error: overflow`.

Any other command (an unknown word, the wrong number of words, a command this version does not offer, wrong case) gives `error: command`. Results are plain text without a trailing newline.

## Interface

Implement this function in `releaser.go` (package `releaser`, module `example.com/releaser`):

```
func Release(version, command string) string
```

* `version`: the version text
* `command`: the command, e.g. `check`, `cmp 1.2.3`, `patch`
* returns the result text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

| version | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| `4.11.7` | `check` | `ok` |
| `8.4.12` | `cmp 1.8.5` | `greater` |
| `6.10.15` | `major` | `7.0.0` |

Run the visible tests with `go test ./...`.

module Releaser
  CHANNELS = ['moss', 'fern', 'oak']
  HAS_BUMP = true
  HAS_PRE = false
  MAXN = 999
  DG = '0123456789'

  def self.num(s)
    return nil if s.length < 1 || s.length > MAXN.to_s.length || !s.each_char.all? { |c| DG.include?(c) } || (s.length > 1 && s[0] == '0')
    v = s.to_i
    v <= MAXN ? v : nil
  end

  def self.parse(v)
    di = v.index('-')
    main = di ? v[0...di] : v
    parts = main.split('.', -1)
    return nil if parts.length != 3
    nums = parts.map { |p| num(p) }
    return nil if nums.include?(nil)
    return [nums[0], nums[1], nums[2], nil, nil] unless di
    pre = v[(di + 1)..]
    dot = pre.index('.')
    return nil unless dot
    ch = pre[0...dot]
    return nil unless CHANNELS.include?(ch)
    nn = num(pre[(dot + 1)..])
    return nil if nn.nil? || nn < 1
    [nums[0], nums[1], nums[2], CHANNELS.index(ch), nn]
  end

  def self.text(t)
    s = "#{t[0]}.#{t[1]}.#{t[2]}"
    s += "-#{CHANNELS[t[3]]}.#{t[4]}" unless t[3].nil?
    s
  end

  def self.key(t)
    [t[0], t[1], t[2], t[3].nil? ? 1 : 0, t[3].nil? ? -1 : t[3], t[4].nil? ? 0 : t[4]]
  end

  def self.release(version, command)
    cur = parse(version)
    return 'error: version' if cur.nil?
    w = command.split(/ /, -1)
    return 'ok' if command == 'check'
    if w.length == 2 && w[0] == 'cmp'
      other = parse(w[1])
      return 'error: other' if other.nil?
      c = key(cur) <=> key(other)
      return c < 0 ? 'less' : c > 0 ? 'greater' : 'equal'
    end
    if HAS_BUMP && %w[major minor patch].include?(command)
      m, n, p = cur[0], cur[1], cur[2]
      if command == 'major'
        m += 1
        n = 0
        p = 0
      elsif command == 'minor'
        n += 1
        p = 0
      elsif cur[3].nil?
        p += 1
      end
      return 'error: overflow' if m > MAXN || n > MAXN || p > MAXN
      return text([m, n, p, nil, nil])
    end
    if HAS_PRE && command == 'release'
      return 'error: not a prerelease' if cur[3].nil?
      return text([cur[0], cur[1], cur[2], nil, nil])
    end
    if HAS_PRE && w.length == 2 && w[0] == 'pre'
      return 'error: channel' unless CHANNELS.include?(w[1])
      ci = CHANNELS.index(w[1])
      if cur[3].nil?
        return 'error: overflow' if cur[2] + 1 > MAXN
        return text([cur[0], cur[1], cur[2] + 1, ci, 1])
      end
      return 'error: downgrade' if ci < cur[3]
      if ci == cur[3]
        return 'error: overflow' if cur[4] + 1 > MAXN
        return text([cur[0], cur[1], cur[2], ci, cur[4] + 1])
      end
      return text([cur[0], cur[1], cur[2], ci, 1])
    end
    'error: command'
  end
end

# Release versions for the Saltmarsh toolkit

The release engineers of the Saltmarsh toolkit use a house version scheme. `release(version, command)` checks versions, compares them and computes the next version.

## Versions

A **version** is `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, optionally followed by a pre-release part `-CHANNEL.N`. Numbers (`MAJOR`, `MINOR`, `PATCH`, `N`) are written in decimal with ASCII digits, no sign, no leading zeros (`0` itself is fine), and may not exceed 999. `N` is at least 1. `CHANNEL` is one of `moss`, `fern`, `oak`, in this order from **lowest to highest**. Examples: `1.4.0`, `0.9.12-moss.3`. Nothing else is a version (no blanks, no `v` prefix, no build metadata).

**Precedence** (used by `cmp`): compare `MAJOR`, then `MINOR`, then `PATCH` numerically; if they are all equal a version **without** a pre-release part is greater than one with it; two pre-release versions compare by channel order, then by `N`.

## Commands

`version` is validated first: if it is not a version the result is `error: version`, whatever the command is. The `command` text is split at **single spaces** (so a doubled or trailing space gives an unknown command). Commands:

* `check`: the result is `ok`.
* `cmp OTHER`: exactly one more word. If `OTHER` is not a version the result is `error: other`; otherwise `less`, `equal` or `greater` (is `version` less than, equal to or greater than `OTHER`).
* `major`: `MAJOR+1.0.0`. `minor`: `MAJOR.MINOR+1.0`. Both drop any pre-release part.
* `patch`: if the version has a pre-release part, only that part is dropped (the version *graduates*: `1.2.4-fern.2` becomes `1.2.4`); otherwise `PATCH` is increased by one.
  Any bump that would make a number exceed 999 gives `error: overflow`.

Any other command (an unknown word, the wrong number of words, a command this version does not offer, wrong case) gives `error: command`. Results are plain text without a trailing newline.

## Interface

Implement this function in `lib/releaser.rb` (module `Releaser`):

```
Releaser.release(version, command)
```

* `version`: the version text
* `command`: the command, e.g. `check`, `cmp 1.2.3`, `patch`
* returns the result text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

| version | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| `9.1.14` | `check` | `ok` |
| `9.4.6` | `cmp 9.10.4` | `less` |
| `0.10.8` | `major` | `1.0.0` |

# Release versions for the Saltmarsh toolkit

The release engineers of the Saltmarsh toolkit use a house version scheme. `release(version, command)` checks versions, compares them and computes the next version.

## Versions

A **version** is `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, optionally followed by a pre-release part `-CHANNEL.N`. Numbers (`MAJOR`, `MINOR`, `PATCH`, `N`) are written in decimal with ASCII digits, no sign, no leading zeros (`0` itself is fine), and may not exceed 9999. `N` is at least 1. `CHANNEL` is one of `ice`, `dew`, `rain`, `storm`, in this order from **lowest to highest**. Examples: `1.4.0`, `0.9.12-ice.3`. Nothing else is a version (no blanks, no `v` prefix, no build metadata).

**Precedence** (used by `cmp`): compare `MAJOR`, then `MINOR`, then `PATCH` numerically; if they are all equal a version **without** a pre-release part is greater than one with it; two pre-release versions compare by channel order, then by `N`.

## Commands

`version` is validated first: if it is not a version the result is `error: version`, whatever the command is. The `command` text is split at **single spaces** (so a doubled or trailing space gives an unknown command). Commands:

* `check`: the result is `ok`.
* `cmp OTHER`: exactly one more word. If `OTHER` is not a version the result is `error: other`; otherwise `less`, `equal` or `greater` (is `version` less than, equal to or greater than `OTHER`).
* `major`: `MAJOR+1.0.0`. `minor`: `MAJOR.MINOR+1.0`. Both drop any pre-release part.
* `patch`: if the version has a pre-release part, only that part is dropped (the version *graduates*: `1.2.4-dew.2` becomes `1.2.4`); otherwise `PATCH` is increased by one.
  Any bump that would make a number exceed 9999 gives `error: overflow`.
* `release`: drops the pre-release part; `error: not a prerelease` if there is none.
* `pre CHANNEL`: `CHANNEL` must be one of the channels (otherwise `error: channel`). If the version has no pre-release part the result is the next patch version with `-CHANNEL.1` (`1.2.3` becomes `1.2.4-ice.1`). If it has a pre-release part: a target channel *lower* than the current one is `error: downgrade`; the *same* channel increases `N` by one; a *higher* channel keeps `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` and restarts at `-CHANNEL.1`. A result with a number above 9999 is `error: overflow` (checked after the other rules).

Any other command (an unknown word, the wrong number of words, a command this version does not offer, wrong case) gives `error: command`. Results are plain text without a trailing newline.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/lib.rs` (library crate `releaser`):

```
pub fn release(version: &str, command: &str) -> String
```

* `version`: the version text
* `command`: the command, e.g. `check`, `cmp 1.2.3`, `patch`, `pre rc`
* returns the result text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

| version | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| `0.10.3` | `check` | `ok` |
| `10.7.3` | `cmp 8.7.10` | `greater` |
| `3.9.10` | `major` | `4.0.0` |

Run the visible tests with `cargo test --offline`.

The release engineers of the Quillfeather client use a house version scheme. `release(version, command)` checks versions, compares them and computes the next version.

## Versions

A **version** is `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, optionally followed by a pre-release part `-CHANNEL.N`. Numbers (`MAJOR`, `MINOR`, `PATCH`, `N`) are written in decimal with ASCII digits, no sign, no leading zeros (`0` itself is fine), and may not exceed 99. `N` is at least 1. `CHANNEL` is one of `dawn`, `noon`, `dusk`, in this order from **lowest to highest**. Examples: `1.4.0`, `0.9.12-dawn.3`. Nothing else is a version (no blanks, no `v` prefix, no build metadata).

**Precedence** (used by `cmp`): compare `MAJOR`, then `MINOR`, then `PATCH` numerically; if they are all equal a version **without** a pre-release part is greater than one with it; two pre-release versions compare by channel order, then by `N`.

## Commands

`version` is validated first: if it is not a version the result is `error: version`, whatever the command is. The `command` text is split at **single spaces** (so a doubled or trailing space gives an unknown command). Commands:

* `check`: the result is `ok`.
* `cmp OTHER`: exactly one more word. If `OTHER` is not a version the result is `error: other`; otherwise `less`, `equal` or `greater` (is `version` less than, equal to or greater than `OTHER`).
* `major`: `MAJOR+1.0.0`. `minor`: `MAJOR.MINOR+1.0`. Both drop any pre-release part.
* `patch`: if the version has a pre-release part, only that part is dropped (the version *graduates*: `1.2.4-noon.2` becomes `1.2.4`); otherwise `PATCH` is increased by one.
  Any bump that would make a number exceed 99 gives `error: overflow`.
* `release`: drops the pre-release part; `error: not a prerelease` if there is none.
* `pre CHANNEL`: `CHANNEL` must be one of the channels (otherwise `error: channel`). If the version has no pre-release part the result is the next patch version with `-CHANNEL.1` (`1.2.3` becomes `1.2.4-dawn.1`). If it has a pre-release part: a target channel *lower* than the current one is `error: downgrade`; the *same* channel increases `N` by one; a *higher* channel keeps `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` and restarts at `-CHANNEL.1`. A result with a number above 99 is `error: overflow` (checked after the other rules).

Any other command (an unknown word, the wrong number of words, a command this version does not offer, wrong case) gives `error: command`. Results are plain text without a trailing newline.

## Interface

Implement this function in `releaser.go` (package `releaser`, module `example.com/releaser`):

```
func Release(version, command string) string
```

* `version`: the version text
* `command`: the command, e.g. `check`, `cmp 1.2.3`, `patch`, `pre rc`
* returns the result text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

| version | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| `9.2.18` | `check` | `ok` |
| `7.4.9` | `cmp 7.11.0` | `less` |
| `7.3.17` | `major` | `8.0.0` |

Run the visible tests with `go test ./...`.

module Releaser
  CHANNELS = ['spark', 'flame', 'blaze', 'ember']
  HAS_BUMP = true
  HAS_PRE = true
  MAXN = 99
  DG = '0123456789'

  def self.num(s)
    return nil if s.length < 1 || s.length > MAXN.to_s.length || !s.each_char.all? { |c| DG.include?(c) } || (s.length > 1 && s[0] == '0')
    v = s.to_i
    v <= MAXN ? v : nil
  end

  def self.parse(v)
    di = v.index('-')
    main = di ? v[0...di] : v
    parts = main.split('.', -1)
    return nil if parts.length != 3
    nums = parts.map { |p| num(p) }
    return nil if nums.include?(nil)
    return [nums[0], nums[1], nums[2], nil, nil] unless di
    pre = v[(di + 1)..]
    dot = pre.index('.')
    return nil unless dot
    ch = pre[0...dot]
    return nil unless CHANNELS.include?(ch)
    nn = num(pre[(dot + 1)..])
    return nil if nn.nil? || nn < 1
    [nums[0], nums[1], nums[2], CHANNELS.index(ch), nn]
  end

  def self.text(t)
    s = "#{t[0]}.#{t[1]}.#{t[2]}"
    s += "-#{CHANNELS[t[3]]}.#{t[4]}" unless t[3].nil?
    s
  end

  def self.key(t)
    [t[0], t[1], t[2], t[3].nil? ? 1 : 0, t[3].nil? ? -1 : t[3], t[4].nil? ? 0 : t[4]]
  end

  def self.release(version, command)
    cur = parse(version)
    return 'error: version' if cur.nil?
    w = command.split(/ /, -1)
    return 'ok' if command == 'check'
    if w.length == 2 && w[0] == 'cmp'
      other = parse(w[1])
      return 'error: other' if other.nil?
      c = key(cur) <=> key(other)
      return c < 0 ? 'less' : c > 0 ? 'greater' : 'equal'
    end
    if HAS_BUMP && %w[major minor patch].include?(command)
      m, n, p = cur[0], cur[1], cur[2]
      if command == 'major'
        m += 1
        n = 0
        p = 0
      elsif command == 'minor'
        n += 1
        p = 0
      elsif cur[3].nil?
        p += 1
      end
      return 'error: overflow' if m > MAXN || n > MAXN || p > MAXN
      return text([m, n, p, nil, nil])
    end
    if HAS_PRE && command == 'release'
      return 'error: not a prerelease' if cur[3].nil?
      return text([cur[0], cur[1], cur[2], nil, nil])
    end
    if HAS_PRE && w.length == 2 && w[0] == 'pre'
      return 'error: channel' unless CHANNELS.include?(w[1])
      ci = CHANNELS.index(w[1])
      if cur[3].nil?
        return 'error: overflow' if cur[2] + 1 > MAXN
        return text([cur[0], cur[1], cur[2] + 1, ci, 1])
      end
      return 'error: downgrade' if ci < cur[3]
      if ci == cur[3]
        return 'error: overflow' if cur[4] + 1 > MAXN
        return text([cur[0], cur[1], cur[2], ci, cur[4] + 1])
      end
      return text([cur[0], cur[1], cur[2], ci, 1])
    end
    'error: command'
  end
end

# Release versions for the Saltmarsh toolkit

The release engineers of the Saltmarsh toolkit use a house version scheme. `release(version, command)` checks versions, compares them and computes the next version.

## Versions

A **version** is `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, optionally followed by a pre-release part `-CHANNEL.N`. Numbers (`MAJOR`, `MINOR`, `PATCH`, `N`) are written in decimal with ASCII digits, no sign, no leading zeros (`0` itself is fine), and may not exceed 99. `N` is at least 1. `CHANNEL` is one of `spark`, `flame`, `blaze`, `ember`, in this order from **lowest to highest**. Examples: `1.4.0`, `0.9.12-spark.3`. Nothing else is a version (no blanks, no `v` prefix, no build metadata).

**Precedence** (used by `cmp`): compare `MAJOR`, then `MINOR`, then `PATCH` numerically; if they are all equal a version **without** a pre-release part is greater than one with it; two pre-release versions compare by channel order, then by `N`.

## Commands

`version` is validated first: if it is not a version the result is `error: version`, whatever the command is. The `command` text is split at **single spaces** (so a doubled or trailing space gives an unknown command). Commands:

* `check`: the result is `ok`.
* `cmp OTHER`: exactly one more word. If `OTHER` is not a version the result is `error: other`; otherwise `less`, `equal` or `greater` (is `version` less than, equal to or greater than `OTHER`).
* `major`: `MAJOR+1.0.0`. `minor`: `MAJOR.MINOR+1.0`. Both drop any pre-release part.
* `patch`: if the version has a pre-release part, only that part is dropped (the version *graduates*: `1.2.4-flame.2` becomes `1.2.4`); otherwise `PATCH` is increased by one.
  Any bump that would make a number exceed 99 gives `error: overflow`.
* `release`: drops the pre-release part; `error: not a prerelease` if there is none.
* `pre CHANNEL`: `CHANNEL` must be one of the channels (otherwise `error: channel`). If the version has no pre-release part the result is the next patch version with `-CHANNEL.1` (`1.2.3` becomes `1.2.4-spark.1`). If it has a pre-release part: a target channel *lower* than the current one is `error: downgrade`; the *same* channel increases `N` by one; a *higher* channel keeps `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` and restarts at `-CHANNEL.1`. A result with a number above 99 is `error: overflow` (checked after the other rules).

Any other command (an unknown word, the wrong number of words, a command this version does not offer, wrong case) gives `error: command`. Results are plain text without a trailing newline.

## Interface

Implement this function in `lib/releaser.rb` (module `Releaser`):

```
Releaser.release(version, command)
```

* `version`: the version text
* `command`: the command, e.g. `check`, `cmp 1.2.3`, `patch`, `pre rc`
* returns the result text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

## Examples

| version | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| `0.4.19` | `check` | `ok` |
| `4.0.2` | `cmp 10.5.18` | `less` |
| `11.1.3` | `major` | `12.0.0` |

# Release versions for the lighthouse dashboard

The release engineers of the lighthouse dashboard use a house version scheme. `release(version, command)` checks versions, compares them and computes the next version.

## Versions

A **version** is `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, optionally followed by a pre-release part `-CHANNEL.N`. Numbers (`MAJOR`, `MINOR`, `PATCH`, `N`) are written in decimal with ASCII digits, no sign, no leading zeros (`0` itself is fine), and may not exceed 999. `N` is at least 1. `CHANNEL` is one of `nightly`, `preview`, `candidate`, in this order from **lowest to highest**. Examples: `1.4.0`, `0.9.12-nightly.3`. Nothing else is a version (no blanks, no `v` prefix, no build metadata).

**Precedence** (used by `cmp`): compare `MAJOR`, then `MINOR`, then `PATCH` numerically; if they are all equal a version **without** a pre-release part is greater than one with it; two pre-release versions compare by channel order, then by `N`.

## Commands

`version` is validated first: if it is not a version the result is `error: version`, whatever the command is. The `command` text is split at **single spaces** (so a doubled or trailing space gives an unknown command). Commands:

* `check`: the result is `ok`.
* `cmp OTHER`: exactly one more word. If `OTHER` is not a version the result is `error: other`; otherwise `less`, `equal` or `greater` (is `version` less than, equal to or greater than `OTHER`).
* `major`: `MAJOR+1.0.0`. `minor`: `MAJOR.MINOR+1.0`. Both drop any pre-release part.
* `patch`: if the version has a pre-release part, only that part is dropped (the version *graduates*: `1.2.4-preview.2` becomes `1.2.4`); otherwise `PATCH` is increased by one.
  Any bump that would make a number exceed 999 gives `error: overflow`.
* `release`: drops the pre-release part; `error: not a prerelease` if there is none.
* `pre CHANNEL`: `CHANNEL` must be one of the channels (otherwise `error: channel`). If the version has no pre-release part the result is the next patch version with `-CHANNEL.1` (`1.2.3` becomes `1.2.4-nightly.1`). If it has a pre-release part: a target channel *lower* than the current one is `error: downgrade`; the *same* channel increases `N` by one; a *higher* channel keeps `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` and restarts at `-CHANNEL.1`. A result with a number above 999 is `error: overflow` (checked after the other rules).

Any other command (an unknown word, the wrong number of words, a command this version does not offer, wrong case) gives `error: command`. Results are plain text without a trailing newline.

## Interface

Implement this function in `src/lib.rs` (library crate `releaser`):

```
pub fn release(version: &str, command: &str) -> String
```

* `version`: the version text
* `command`: the command, e.g. `check`, `cmp 1.2.3`, `patch`, `pre rc`
* returns the result text.

All inputs and the result are plain strings. Invalid input is reported *inside the result text* as the rules in this document say; the function itself never throws, panics or exits.

| `1.9.13` | `cmp 5.8.6` | `less` |
| `3.5.19` | `major` | `4.0.0` |
